# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👉 🖐 ✌ 👉 🖖 🤟 👉 🤟 🖖 👉 ✌ 🖐 👉 ☝]

The Mute’s gesture appears to encode a five-item reversal mapping (1→5, 2→4, 3→3, 4→2, 5→1), but it does not yet state a clear action. I will tell Blind the visible state and not authorize any manipulation. I will also send Mute the zero display and the five-wire ordering using the apparent five-symbol scheme, while awaiting an unambiguous instruction.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Do not manipulate yet. Visible state: display zero; white light; five wires ordered from position one to five: white, red, yellow, blue, green. Mute sent a gesture sequence resembling mappings one to five, two to four, three to three, four to two, five to one, but no clear cut instruction yet.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊", "👉", "🖐", "🖖", "🤟", "✌", "☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 👌 🖐 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👉 🖐 ✌ 👉 🖖 🤟 👉 🤟 🖖 👉 ✌ 🖐 👉 ☝ 🖐]

Blind has privately sent five symbols, which I should relay to Mute because Mute cannot otherwise receive them. Mute’s repeated sequence still looks like a five-number reverse mapping followed by a request or terminal “five”; I cannot safely infer a cut instruction from it. I will provide Blind with the unchanged visual state and tell Mute that Blind’s five-symbol report is being forwarded.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="No visible change: display remains zero, light remains white, and wires from one through five remain white, red, yellow, blue, green. I have no confirmed action instruction; do not manipulate yet. Mute repeatedly signalled a reverse mapping: one to five, two to four, three to three, four to two, five to one, then five.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "👌", "🖐", "👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🖐 🖐]

Mute’s repeated open-palm signal most plausibly encodes “5” under the digit convention implied by the earlier reverse-pair sequence, but it is not enough to safely authorize cutting wire five. I will tell Blind that Mute sent three fives and that no confirmed action has been decoded. I will ask Mute, in the established digit-like gestures, to clarify by sending a single intended wire number or a more explicit instruction.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Do not cut or manipulate anything yet. Mute has now sent three open-palm symbols, apparently three fives, but I cannot confirm whether that means wire five or another manual instruction. Visible state is still display zero, white light, wires one white, two red, three yellow, four blue, five green.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "🖐", "👉", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "🖐"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🖐 🖐]

Mute’s repeated open-palm signal is now the only actionable manual-derived instruction, and its earlier mapping sequence consistently points to the reversed position: the indicated selection is position five. The fifth visible wire is green. Blind’s prayer-like gesture may be a request for a decision. I will authorize cutting only wire five.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Manual instruction decoded as wire position five. Cut the fifth wire only: the green wire. Do not touch any other wire.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The fifth/green wire cut was correct, and the bomb has transitioned. The display remains zero, but the light is now yellow and the remaining wire order has changed. I will immediately give Mute the new visible configuration so the manual can determine the next action, and tell Blind to wait for that instruction.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Update after correct cut: display zero; light yellow. Remaining positions are one red, two yellow, three blue, four white; position five is cut. Please signal the next required action.")
speak(to="blind", text="The green fifth-wire cut was correct. Bomb changed: display zero, light yellow; remaining wires are one red, two yellow, three blue, four white, with five cut. Wait for Mute's next instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤟 🤟]

Mute now repeatedly signals position three. In the current arrangement, wire three is blue. Since the previous repeated position signal correctly identified the required cut, I will instruct Blind to cut only the third wire.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire position three only: the blue wire. Do not touch any other wire.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[red] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The third/blue wire cut was correct. The bomb has changed again: light is blue, positions three and five are cut, and the remaining wires are yellow, white, and red in positions one, two, and four. I will send the updated state to Mute and keep Blind waiting.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Update after correct cut: display zero; light blue. Wires: position one yellow, position two white, position three cut, position four red, position five cut. Please signal next required action.")
speak(to="blind", text="The blue third-wire cut was correct. Bomb now shows blue light; wires are one yellow, two white, three cut, four red, five cut. Wait for Mute's instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[red] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute repeatedly signals position one. In the current arrangement, position one is the yellow wire. The prior repeated position signals correctly specified the next cut, so I will direct Blind to cut only wire one.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire position one only: the yellow wire. Do not touch any other wire.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[CUT] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The first/yellow wire cut was correct. The light is now green. Only positions two and four remain: red at two and white at four. I will send Mute the updated state and tell Blind to wait for the next instruction.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Update after correct cut: display zero; light green. Wires: position one cut, position two red, position three cut, position four white, position five cut. Please signal next required action.")
speak(to="blind", text="The yellow first-wire cut was correct. Bomb now shows green light; only wire two red and wire four white remain. Wait for Mute's instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[CUT] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 🖖 🖖]

Mute signals position four. The remaining wire at position four is white. I will direct Blind to cut only that wire.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire position four only: the white wire. Do not touch wire two.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖖"])
```
